text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Some 10,000 small, independent insurance agents set up IAB bank IAB to settle their payments in bid to ward off attacks by large financial groups. (p1)
- Pharmacy chains Etos, Kruidvat and DA slug it out in bid to bring independent chemists under their control. (p1)
- Foreign Affairs Minister Hans van Mierlo wants broader EU-US dialogue, not just business and trade. (p1)
- Steel group Hoogovens still at odds with unions over jobs guarantee. (1)
- European information and communication sector rapidly losing ground to rivals from Japan, Korea and U.S. -survey. (p1)
- Reed Elsevier buys U.S. legal publishing activities (p3)
- Retail trade set to double its use of technological gadgetry, such as "intelligent" client card -- Moret Ernst & Young. (p7)
- Amsterdam's Schiphol airport could have throughput of 85 million passengers a year by 2020 -- planning bureau. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- European economy seriously lagging behind U.S. and Japan - report (p1)
- Shareholders in bankrupt sports-only TV channel Sport 7 still in race for soccer broadcast rights. (p1)
- Rotterdam port firm European Bulk Services (EBS) goes to court in attempt to force unions to accept job cuts. (p2)
- Dutch drank Dfl 2.5 billion worth of wine last year, a rise of eight percent on 1995. (p2)
- Third quarter 1996 job vacancies fell by 10,000 (p31)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Financial watchdog (ECD) uncovers multi-million guilder health service fraud. (p1)
- Netherlands on alert against flu epidemic. (p1)
- Employers association (VNO-NCW) chairman urges national pact of employers, unions and state against unemployment. (p29)
- Food and drinks group BolsWessanen enters Asian market. (p29)
TROUW
- ING insurance unit RVS targets better-off ethnic minorities, particularly Turks. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Rising dollar boosts Dutch corporate profits. (p1)
- Department store chain KBB fires director of loss-making fashion unit M&S Mode. (p11)
